questions.stem:
(a) Define each of the following: (i) tourism; (ii) tourist; (iii) excursionist; (iv) hospitality. [8 marks]
(b) Distinguish between domestic and international tourism. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the following forms of tourism: (i) eco-tourism; (ii) religious tourism; (iii) business tourism; (iv) cultural tourism. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) tourism: the activities of people travelling to and staying in places outside their usual environment for leisure, business or other purposes, and the services provided for them
2 marks: (a)(ii) tourist: a visitor who stays at least one night away from home at the destination
2 marks: (a)(iii) excursionist: a same-day visitor who does not stay overnight
2 marks: (a)(iv) hospitality: friendly reception and provision of accommodation, food and drink to guests
2 marks: (b) domestic tourism: travel by residents within their own country
2 marks: (b) international tourism: travel across national borders (inbound and outbound)
2 marks: (c)(i) eco-tourism: responsible travel to natural areas that conserves the environment
2 marks: (c)(ii) religious tourism: travel for pilgrimage or religious events
2 marks: (c)(iii) business tourism: travel for meetings, conferences and trade
2 marks: (c)(iv) cultural tourism: travel to experience the culture, festivals, arts and heritage of a people
questions.explanation: Tourism is travel and stay away from the usual environment and the services for it. A tourist stays overnight; an excursionist does not. Hospitality is welcoming and serving guests. Domestic tourism is within one's country; international crosses borders. Eco, religious, business and cultural tourism are defined by purpose.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between natural and man-made tourist attractions, giving two examples of each from Nigeria. [8 marks]
(b) State the location (state) of each of the following attractions: (i) Obudu Mountain Resort; (ii) Ikogosi Warm Springs; (iii) Gidan Makama Museum; (iv) Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove. [8 marks]
(c) State two ways of preserving tourist attractions. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) natural attractions are created by nature
2 marks: (a) examples of natural: e.g. Yankari National Park, Olumo Rock, Erin Ijesha waterfalls, Zuma Rock, Bar Beach
2 marks: (a) man-made attractions are built or created by people
2 marks: (a) examples of man-made: e.g. National Museum, palaces, National Theatre, monuments
2 marks: (b)(i) Cross River State
2 marks: (b)(ii) Ekiti State
2 marks: (b)(iii) Kano State
2 marks: (b)(iv) Osun State
4 marks: (c) any two, 2 marks each: laws against destruction; regular maintenance; public enlightenment; fencing and security; controlled visitor numbers; funding by government
questions.explanation: Natural attractions (Yankari, Olumo Rock) are made by nature; man-made ones (museums, palaces) by people. Obudu is in Cross River, Ikogosi in Ekiti, Gidan Makama in Kano and the Osun-Osogbo Grove in Osun. Preservation needs laws, maintenance, security and public enlightenment.

questions.stem:
(a) State four economic benefits of tourism to a nation. [8 marks]
(b) State three social benefits of tourism. [6 marks]
(c) State three developmental benefits of tourism to rural communities. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) any four, 2 marks each: foreign exchange earnings; government revenue from taxes and levies; employment; improved balance of payments; income for local businesses; attracts investment
6 marks: (b) any three, 2 marks each: promotes cultural understanding; job creation reduces social vices; international co-operation and friendship; preservation of culture; education
6 marks: (c) any three, 2 marks each: roads; electricity; water supply; communication facilities; new buildings and markets; preservation of nature and land use
questions.explanation: Tourism earns foreign exchange, raises tax revenue, creates jobs and improves the balance of payments. Socially it promotes understanding and preserves culture. It also brings roads, power, water and communication to rural areas.

questions.topic: Festivals and Heritages in a Nation
questions.stem:
(a) Describe each of the following festivals and state where it is held: (i) Argungu Fishing Festival; (ii) Osun-Osogbo Festival; (iii) New Yam Festival. [12 marks]
(b) Explain the meaning of a heritage site and give two examples in Nigeria. [4 marks]
(c) State two ways festivals promote tourism. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a)(i) a fishing contest in which fishermen catch fish by hand and with nets in the river, with cultural displays; held in Argungu, Kebbi State
4 marks: (a)(ii) an annual festival in honour of the Osun river goddess with a procession to the sacred grove; held in Osogbo, Osun State
4 marks: (a)(iii) a harvest festival celebrating the new yam and thanksgiving; held in many Igbo communities (and other parts of Nigeria)
2 marks: (b) a place of cultural or natural importance preserved for present and future generations
2 marks: (b) any two examples: Sukur Cultural Landscape; Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove; Gidan Makama Museum; national museums; palaces (1 mark each)
4 marks: (c) any two, 2 marks each: attract local and foreign visitors; generate income for hosts; showcase culture; boost hotels and transport businesses; publicity for the destination
questions.explanation: Argungu (Kebbi) is a fishing contest; Osun-Osogbo (Osun) honours the river goddess; the New Yam Festival marks the harvest, especially in Igbo land. Heritage sites such as Sukur and the Osun-Osogbo Grove are preserved for their value. Festivals draw visitors, income and publicity.

questions.stem:
(a) Define a tour operator. [2 marks]
(b) Explain three roles of a tour operator. [6 marks]
(c) State four qualities of a good tour operator. [4 marks]
(d) State four functions of a travel agent. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a business that assembles the components of a holiday (transport, accommodation, activities) into packages and sells them
2 marks: (b) packaging: combining transport, accommodation and activities into a single product
2 marks: (b) marketing: promoting and selling the packages through brochures, media and agents
2 marks: (b) executing: operating the tour, providing guides and ensuring the services are delivered
4 marks: (c) any four: honesty; good public relations; marketing skills; financial strength; knowledge of destinations; innovativeness; ICT skills (1 mark each)
8 marks: (d) any four, 2 marks each: reservation; ticketing; visa procurement; foreign exchange procurement; travel advice and information; selling package tours; arranging travel insurance
questions.explanation: A tour operator packages, markets and executes tours. Good operators are honest, creative, financially sound, skilled in marketing and ICT and know their destinations. Travel agents make reservations, issue tickets, procure visas and foreign exchange and give travel advice.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and answer the questions.
Mrs Ngozi Eze runs a small workshop in Enugu where she and four apprentices produce beaded jewellery, raffia bags and tie-dye fabrics. Most of her customers are tourists who visit a nearby resort. She advertises on social media and displays her goods at a local craft fair.
(a) What type of industry does Mrs Eze run? Give a reason. [4 marks]
(b) Name four other cottage industries that can supply the tourism sector. [4 marks]
(c) Identify two tourism marketing tools used by Mrs Eze. [4 marks]
(d) State four ways her business benefits tourism and the local community. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) cottage industry
2 marks: (a) reason: small-scale, home/workshop based, handmade crafts with few workers
4 marks: (b) any four: leather works; ceramics and pottery; bread making; hair weaving; painting; cloth weaving; cane furniture; wood carving (1 mark each)
4 marks: (c) social media (e-tourism) and craft fair/exhibition (2 marks each)
8 marks: (d) any four, 2 marks each: provides souvenirs for tourists; creates jobs/apprenticeship; preserves local crafts and culture; generates income; promotes the destination; skill acquisition for youths
questions.explanation: Mrs Eze runs a cottage industry because it is small-scale and handmade. Others include leather work, pottery, weaving and wood carving. She uses social media and craft fairs. Her business supplies souvenirs, creates jobs, preserves crafts and promotes the destination.
